gaps.sentence: ___ of the two proposals has been approved so far.
gaps.explanation: 'Neither of the two' — 'none' is for three or more.

gaps.sentence: He was driving ___ fast for the icy road.
gaps.explanation: 'Too fast for something' means faster than is safe; 'so fast' needs a 'that' clause, not 'for'.

gaps.sentence: She gave the children two sweets ___.
gaps.hint: distribution per child at the end of the sentence
gaps.explanation: 'Two sweets each' means two per child; 'every' cannot stand alone here.

gaps.sentence: ___ of the workforce is part-time now.
gaps.hint: pattern: ___ of + specific group; singular verb
gaps.explanation: 'Half of the workforce is ...' is the correct pattern; 'the half of' is not used in this position.

gaps.sentence: We see our grandparents ___ other weekend.
gaps.explanation: 'Every other weekend' means alternate weekends; 'each other' has a different, reciprocal meaning.
'Cut something in half' is the fixed expression; 'in middle' would need 'the middle'.

gaps.sentence: I'd like ___ more time to think about your offer.
gaps.explanation: 'A little more time' means a small additional amount; 'time' is uncountable so 'a few' is wrong.

gaps.sentence: ___ candidate was given five minutes to speak.
gaps.hint: one at a time, singular verb
gaps.explanation: 'Each candidate was given' — singular agreement; 'all candidate' is wrong.
